records.text: Heliodorus offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made very great vows to the One who had preserved his life. He warmly took leave of Onias and departed with his company to the king.
As my life was failing me, I remembered the Lord; may my prayer come to Thee, into Thy holy sanctuary.
Those who guard vain and false things abandoned their mercy.
But I, with a voice of praise and thanksgiving, will sacrifice to Thee. Whatever I vowed I will repay to Thee, for deliverance to the Lord!”

that the priests were no longer eager for the services of the altar. Despising the temple and neglecting the sacrifices, they hurried to take part in the unlawful provision of exercises in the wrestling ground after the signal for the discus.

“A son honors his father, and a slave his master. If I am a father, where is My honor? If I am a master, where is the fear of Me?” says the Lord Almighty. You priests who belittle My name! But you said, “How have we belittled Thy name?”
“By bringing polluted loaves to My altar.” But you said, “How have we polluted them?” “By your saying, ‘The Lord’s table is despised, and the foods placed upon it are despised.’”

“For if you bring a blind animal for sacrifice, is that not evil? If you bring one that is lame or sick, is that not evil? Bring it, then, to your ruler! Will he accept it? Will he show you favor?” says the Lord Almighty.
Antiochus was deeply grieved, moved to pity, and wept because of the deceased man’s self-restraint and admirable conduct.
David said to Joab and all the people with him, “Tear your garments, put on sackcloth, and beat yourselves in mourning before Abner.” King David walked behind the bier.
They buried Abner in Hebron. The king lifted his voice and wept at his grave, and all the people wept over Abner.
The king lamented over Abner and said, “Should Abner die according to Nabal’s death?
Your hands were not bound; your feet were not in fetters. He did not bring near, as Nabal; before men of injustice you fell.” All the people gathered to weep over him.
He who had thrown out multitudes unburied went unmourned and received neither any funeral care whatever nor a place in his ancestral tomb.
Therefore thus says the Lord concerning Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: Woe upon this man! They will certainly not mourn him, O brother! Nor will they weep for him, Alas, lord!
He will be buried with a donkey’s burial; swept up, he will be thrown beyond Jerusalem’s gate.
There was killing of young and old, destruction of boys, women and children, and slaughter of virgins and infants.
To these others He said while I listened, “Go behind him into the city and strike. Do not spare with your eyes, and have no mercy.

Old man, young man, maiden, infants and women—kill them to obliteration. But do not approach anyone upon whom the sign is. Begin at My holy places.” They began with the elderly men who were inside the house.

But he adopted a noble resolve, worthy of his age, the dignity of his old age, his acquired and distinguished gray hair, his excellent conduct from childhood, and still more the holy legislation established by God. Accordingly he declared at once that they should send him to Hades.
Old age is a crown of boasting, and it is found in ways of righteousness.
How fitting is judgment for gray hair, and knowledge of counsel for elders!
How fitting is wisdom for the old, and thought and counsel for the honored!
Long experience is the crown of the old, and their boast is the fear of the Lord.

triples.relationship: Sacrifice and vows after danger to life
triples.rationale: Heliodorus sacrifices and makes vows to the One who preserved his life after his near-fatal ordeal. Jonah recalls his failing life and promises thankful sacrifice and repayment of his vows while praying for deliverance. Both connect endangered life, appeal to the Lord, sacrifice and vows; Heliodorus's enacted offering and Jonah's promised offering remain distinct.

triples.rationale: The priests in Maccabees despise the temple and neglect its sacrifices in favour of athletic exercises. Malachi rebukes priests who belittle God's name and treat His table as despised by bringing polluted and defective offerings. Both condemn priests' contempt for their altar responsibilities, with neglect for athletics distinguished from the presentation of unacceptable offerings.

triples.relationship: Royal mourning for a man unjustly killed
triples.rationale: Antiochus weeps over Onias after learning of his unjust murder and admiring his conduct. David leads mourning for Abner, weeps at his grave and laments his fall before men of injustice. Both narratives show a king grieving an unjust killing, without equating the victims, their offices or the kings' later treatment of the killers.

triples.relationship: Loss of mourning and honourable burial
triples.rationale: Jason, who left others unburied, receives neither mourning nor funeral care or an ancestral tomb. Jeremiah announces that Jehoiakim will not be mourned and will receive a dishonourable burial outside Jerusalem's gate. Both portray deprivation of mourning and proper burial as an ignominious end, without identifying Jason with Jehoiakim or assigning the same disposal of the body to both.

triples.relationship: Comparison of lists describing slaughter across age and sex
triples.rationale: The massacre narrative lists young and old, women, children, virgins and infants among those killed. Ezekiel's vision similarly lists old men, young men, maidens, infants and women in the order to strike Jerusalem. The shared enumeration conveys the breadth of the killing; the vision explicitly exempts those bearing the sign, and Antiochus's soldiers are not identified with its agents or granted its divine commission.

triples.relationship: Wisdom principle linking honourable age and righteousness
triples.rationale: Eleazar judges his resolve by the dignity of old age and his lifelong excellent conduct, with God's law foremost. Proverbs calls old age a crown of boasting found in ways of righteousness. The narrative embodies the connection between honourable age and righteous conduct; the proverb does not name Eleazar or prescribe his particular martyrdom.

triples.relationship: Wisdom principle of conduct fitting gray hair
triples.rationale: Eleazar's resolve is described as worthy of his age and distinguished gray hair alongside his excellent conduct from childhood. Sirach calls judgment, wisdom and counsel fitting for gray hair and elders, and names fear of the Lord their boast. Both link the honour of age to moral and discerning conduct, without claiming Sirach describes Eleazar's biography or commands his particular decision.
